items.title: Grover Mitchell interviewed by Monk Rowe, Sarasota, Florida, February 13, 1996
items.q: maybe like Al Grey, you know, just to play one solo on one track.

ctx.x: Well you’ve been a part of some of the greatest music making and what was it like playing with Duke?

Oh, no, it was great. He was something else man, he was really bright. You know he was a special case. You know I’d have to sit here a week to tell you about Duke Ellington. I could tell you a lot about Basie but Duke was great. He was great. He was great, now we’ve got another one, Quincy Jones, but these guys were great at pulling people together and pulling talent together and making things happen you know? These guys can really see this little tiny thing in one guy and they’d really magnify it and all of a…
He knew what every person could do and what their strong point was.
